title: United States blocks transactions with Russian central bank and sovereign funds
body:
On 28 February 2022 the United States Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new sanctions on Russia's sovereign financial institutions. A new directive issued under Executive Order 14024 prohibited U.S. persons from engaging in any transaction involving the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the National Wealth Fund of the Russian Federation or the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation.

The measure effectively immobilised Central Bank assets held in the United States or by U.S. persons. It followed the 26 February joint statement by Western leaders that committed them to restricting the central bank's use of its international reserves. OFAC also issued a general license permitting certain energy-related transactions with the Central Bank.

On the same day OFAC blocked the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), a sovereign wealth fund, along with its management company JSC RDIF and a subsidiary, LLC RVC Management Company. RDIF's chief executive, Kirill Dmitriev, was also designated. The action was one of several steps taken in the first week of the invasion to limit Russia's access to the international financial system and to the foreign-currency reserves the central bank had accumulated.
